planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in fast-draining, sandy mix after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: Candy Stripe produces waxy flowers in a pinwheel pattern of creamy white and blush-pink stripes blending into a golden-yellow throat, with a sweet classic frangipani fragrance. Like other Plumeria rubra selections it is winter-deciduous and must be kept completely dry through dormancy; in zone 9a, overwinter container specimens in a frost-free, unwatered spot and resume watering only after new growth appears in spring. Give it full sun and excellent drainage, since soggy soil in cool weather is the most common cause of stem and root rot.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry

planting.note: Root cuttings in dry, sandy mix after danger of frost has passed; this selection can be slower to root than other plumeria.

directions: Donald Angus bears cherry-pink, three-inch flowers streaked with white and centered with a large orange-yellow eye, carrying a mild, sweet frangipani fragrance. It is an upright, open-growing tree that blooms heavily and holds its flowers well, though cuttings can be slower to root and the plant is notably cold-sensitive. Like other Plumeria rubra hybrids it drops its leaves and goes fully dormant in winter and must be kept completely dry through that rest; in zone 9a, overwinter container plants in a frost-free, unwatered location.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry

planting.note: Roots readily from dry cuttings in sandy mix; plant after soil has warmed in spring.

directions: Daisy Wilcox opens light pink and quickly fades to large, creamy-white, 4-plus-inch blooms with a strong yellow throat, a pink-edged petal margin, and a spicy fragrance. It is a tall, upright, well-branched grower that flowers abundantly from spring through fall and has long served as a parent plant for other well-known named cultivars. As a deciduous Plumeria rubra selection it drops its leaves and must be kept bone-dry through winter dormancy; in zone 9a, overwinter container specimens in a frost-free, unwatered spot.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in fast-draining soil once frost danger has passed; this selection is notably rust-resistant.

directions: San Germain produces pure-white, star-shaped flowers with pointed petals and a golden throat that glows more intensely in hot weather, carrying one of the most powerful honeysuckle-and-jasmine-like fragrances of any plumeria. It grows upright and well-branched, tends toward evergreen habit in warm climates, and is notably resistant to frangipani rust even when neighboring plants are infected. In zone 9a grow it in a container, withholding water through any winter leaf-drop and protecting it from frost, since it has no cold hardiness.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in fast-draining soil after frost danger passes; this selection wants more consistent moisture than most plumeria to flower well.

directions: Bali Whirl is an Indonesian double-flowered selection bearing roughly ten yellow petals edged in white around a bright yellow center, with a sweet jasmine-like fragrance echoing its presumed parent, the classic yellow cultivar Celadine. It is a robust, medium-sized grower whose flowers are sterile and produce no viable pollen. Like other plumeria it drops its leaves and rests through the cool season; in zone 9a, keep container plants dry and frost-free through winter dormancy and resume watering as new growth appears in spring.

planting.note: Easy to root from dry cuttings in sandy mix after soil has warmed; a fast, compact grower.

directions: Lemon Drop, registered through the Plumeria Society of America and also sold as Thornton's Lemon Drop, bears bright, wide-petaled yellow flowers that pick up a thin white edge with age and carry a strong, true lemon fragrance. It is a compact, heavy-blooming, fast-growing selection well suited to container culture. Like other deciduous plumeria it drops its leaves and goes dormant in winter and must be kept dry during that rest; in zone 9a, overwinter container plants in a frost-free, unwatered spot and resume watering once new growth appears.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry

planting.note: Plant dry, rooted cuttings in sandy mix once frost danger has passed; this is one of the more drought-tolerant named cultivars.

directions: Puu Kahea is one of the Plumeria Society of America's original registered cultivars, carrying star-shaped, elongated yellow-and-white petals striped with red bands that deepen toward wine-pink as the bloom ages, and a fragrance that shifts from mild to a tangy lemon scent. It grows as a compact, well-branched, medium-sized tree that thrives in heat and tolerates drought better than many plumeria. As a deciduous selection it must be kept completely dry through winter dormancy; in zone 9a, overwinter container plants in a frost-free, unwatered location.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in fast-draining soil after frost danger passes; this cultivar is a notably vigorous, fast-growing selection.

directions: Jeannie Moragne bears some of the largest blooms in the genus, five inches or more across, in vivid red fading to reddish pink with broad golden-yellow bands and pink-orange lines radiating to the petal edges, carrying a strong, fruity, rose-like scent. It is one of the historic Moragne-line hybrids from Kauai and grows rapidly, often needing more frequent pruning than other named cultivars to stay in bounds. Like other Plumeria rubra hybrids it drops its leaves and goes fully dormant in winter and must be kept completely dry through that rest; in zone 9a, overwinter container specimens in a frost-free, unwatered spot.
sources: Plumeria Society of America cultivar registry
